subject.title: fix: setup fails closed for invalid configuration arguments

question: Should SetupEngine unconditionally reject duplicate, missing, blank, and flag-looking values for all nine value-taking options, even though automation that previously relied on permissive first-value or fallback behavior will stop with exit code 2?
rationale: The safety benefit is strong because the old fallback can start destructive setup defaults, but this is also an intentional strict-validation compatibility change whose permanent CLI contract requires maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Accept fail-closed CLI contract
options.body: Keep strict validation for all value-taking options and merge after real Windows process proof confirms invalid input cannot begin cleanup or setup.

options.title: Narrow the compatibility change
options.body: Fail closed for explicit configuration errors while preserving or separately deprecating formerly tolerated duplicate and dash-prefixed values for unrelated options.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed CLI contract
